memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "But God did not raise his hand against these leaders of the Israelites; they saw God, and they ate and drank." - Exodus 24:11 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse quietly overflows with grace. Sinful men stood in the presence of the holy God — and He did not strike them down. Instead, something remarkable happened: they ate and drank in His presence. A meal, in that culture, meant friendship, peace, acceptance. God did not merely spare them; He hosted them at His table.

Pause on the wonder of it. These were ordinary men, no more righteous than we are. By every right, God's holiness could have consumed them. But He held back His hand and welcomed them into fellowship. The text almost seems surprised by it — "he did not raise his hand" — as if to underline that this was mercy, not entitlement. Every moment we spend in God's presence is a gift of grace, never something we have earned.

And this meal points forward. Jesus ate with sinners throughout His ministry, scandalising the religious by welcoming the unworthy to His table. Through His sacrifice, He has made a way for us not only to be spared but to be seated as friends of God. One day we will share the marriage supper of the Lamb (Rev 19:9). Until then, remember that every time you come to God, you come as a welcomed guest, not a trespasser. His hand is not raised against you; His table is set for you.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I approach God as a welcomed guest, or as someone fearing rejection?
Am I amazed by the grace that lets me come freely into God's presence?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, by every right You could have turned me away, yet You welcome me to Your table. Thank You for such grace, and let me never take Your presence for granted. Amen.
